title: Garage contract
description: Language-neutral garage/vehicle shapes shared by iOS, Android, backend, and admin. vehicle mirrors the Firestore `vehicles/{vehicleId}` document (docs/firebase-data-model.md), which is authenticated-readable by design. `registrationPlate` is a DELIBERATELY PUBLIC, user-entered field (Seb product decision 2026-07): the owner opts in by filling the field, and it is then readable by ANY signed-in user — the `vehicles` read rule is `isAuthenticated()`, so it is gated on neither membership nor a suspension check. Represented here on purpose. It is the one exception — VIN, insurance data, and vehicle location remain unrepresentable and must never be added, as those were never intended to be public. Garage write callables use `requireActiveActor` (signed-in, not suspended, not deleted) — managing your own garage is deliberately NOT member-gated, and member gating is currently DISABLED repo-wide (`MEMBER_GATING_ENABLED = false` in functions/src/shared/memberGating.ts). Each user may have at most 10 vehicles. Firestore stores timestamps as native Timestamp values; this contract describes their ISO 8601 JSON serialization.

catalogueId.description: A stable machine id from contracts/vehicles/vehicle-catalogue.json, or the reserved `other` ("not listed") bucket. Shape only — MEMBERSHIP is validated server-side against the catalogue (functions/src/garage/vehicle-catalogue.ts), which no JSON-Schema pattern can express. Model ids are unique only WITHIN a manufacturer (`3` exists under both Mazda and MG), so a modelId is meaningful only together with its makeId, and the pair is validated together.

vehiclePowertrain.description: Powertrain type ACCEPTED on the wire and stored in Firestore (functions/src/garage/garage-core.ts VEHICLE_POWERTRAINS). Clients OFFER only the first four (SELECTABLE_VEHICLE_POWERTRAINS: petrol, diesel, hybrid, electric). `plug_in_hybrid` and `other` are retired: no client offers them, but they are still accepted and stored verbatim so vehicles created before the four-option change are neither corrupted nor dropped, and shipped clients that still send them keep working.

vehicle.description: Firestore `vehicles/{vehicleId}`. Any authenticated user can read; all writes go through the member-only garage.* callables.

make.description: Human-readable manufacturer, and the field every reader renders (garage list, public car profile, live main-car mirror, map marker subtitle, admin web). For a structured vehicle it is DERIVED server-side from `makeId`'s catalogue display name, so it can never contradict the id; for a pre-catalogue vehicle it is the owner's original free text, left exactly as they typed it. Never aggregate on this — aggregate on `makeId`.

model.description: Human-readable model; same derivation rules as `make`. When the owner selects the `other` model bucket on a pre-catalogue vehicle, the existing text is KEPT rather than replaced by a placeholder, so no member's only description of their car is destroyed.

makeId.description: Catalogue manufacturer id — THE aggregation key ("how many Volvos does the community own?"). `other` means the owner selected "Other / not listed" because their brand is not in the catalogue: an explicit, countable bucket rather than unparseable prose. null means the vehicle was written on the legacy free-text path (created before this field, or by a shipped client), so it is simply outside the aggregate — `makeId == null` queries exactly the unmapped set. NOT in `required`: pre-catalogue documents omit the field entirely, and none of them are backfilled or fuzzy-matched, because a wrong mapping is worse than an unmapped car.

modelId.description: Catalogue model id within `makeId`. `other` with a REAL makeId is the actionable catalogue-growth signal ("someone owns a Volvo whose model we do not list"); `other` with `makeId: 'other'` is a count-only signal. null on the legacy path. Written together with `makeId` and never independently. NOT in `required` (see makeId).

catalogueVersion.description: The catalogue release (contracts/vehicles/vehicle-catalogue.json `version`) the ids were selected from, taken from the SERVER's own catalogue and never from the client's claim. Gives every aggregate provenance and makes a later catalogue expansion auditable. null whenever makeId/modelId are null. NOT in `required` (see makeId).

modelYear.description: Model year. A STRUCTURED write (makeId present) is held to the window the selector offers — `minModelYear … currentYear + maxModelYearOffset` from contracts/vehicles/vehicle-catalogue.json, i.e. 1900…currentYear+1 — evaluated against the server clock. The legacy free-text path keeps its wider 1886…currentYear+2 bound so no shipped client and no existing vehicle becomes unsaveable.

registrationPlate.description: Deliberately PUBLIC, user-entered registration plate (Seb product decision) — shown on the car profile and readable by any signed-in user (the `vehicles` read rule is `isAuthenticated()`, NOT member-gated). Server-normalised (trim / collapse internal whitespace / uppercase), format-agnostic so imports and personalised plates are accepted (no country regex). null / omitted when the owner left it blank. OPTIONAL and NOT in `required`: vehicles created before this field omit it. FUTURE: an automatic vehicle-info lookup keyed on this plate would slot in as a garage.lookupVehicleByPlate callable — not built yet.

imagePath.description: COVER photo: a denormalised mirror of photoPaths[0], kept for backward compatibility (shipped clients + the profile card read this). Cloud Storage path under vehicleImages/{uid}/{vehicleId}/; null when the vehicle has no photos. Maintained together with photoPaths by every garage.* photo callable.

photoPaths.description: Ordered photo gallery — the SOURCE OF TRUTH for the vehicle's photos; the cover is photoPaths[0] (mirrored into imagePath). Each entry is a Cloud Storage path that MUST lie under vehicleImages/{uid}/{vehicleId}/ (one segment below the prefix; validated server-side against the authenticated uid, so it is not expressible as a JSON-schema pattern). At most 10 photos. OPTIONAL and NOT in `required`: vehicles created before this field omit it and are read as [imagePath] (or [] when imagePath is null). Written only by garage.addVehiclePhoto/removeVehiclePhoto/reorderVehiclePhotos and the imagePath reconcile in garage.updateVehicle.

isMainCar.description: True for the caller's single main car (at most one per user, enforced by garage.setMainVehicle). Its photo is shown as the garage header image. Optional: legacy vehicle docs created before this field existed omit it and must be treated as false.

addVehicleRequest.description:
Input for garage.addVehicle (max 10 vehicles per user). Exactly ONE identity form must be used, and mixing them is rejected outright (a request carrying both is always a client bug, and silently preferring one would store a document whose text and ids disagree):

1. STRUCTURED — `makeId` + `modelId`, what every current client sends. The caller SELECTS both from the catalogue; the server validates the pair against contracts/vehicles/vehicle-catalogue.json and DERIVES the stored `make`/`model` display text itself, so a client cannot label a `volvo` id "Ferrari".
2. LEGACY — `make` + `model` free text, what shipped clients send. Still accepted verbatim so those builds keep working; leaves makeId/modelId null, i.e. the vehicle stays outside the aggregate.

Neither identity form appears in `required`, because "exactly one of two groups" is not expressible here without a oneOf that code generators mangle. The server enforces it (functions/src/garage/garage-core.ts refineVehicleIdentity) and rejects a request that names neither.

makeId.description: Catalogue manufacturer id, or `other` for "not listed". Sent together with modelId. Mutually exclusive with make/model.

modelId.description: Catalogue model id within makeId, or `other`. `makeId: 'other'` accepts only `modelId: 'other'` — once the brand is unknown there is no model list, and a real model id under an unknown brand would produce nonsense pairs in the aggregate.

make.description: LEGACY free-text manufacturer (shipped clients only). Mutually exclusive with makeId/modelId; must be sent together with `model` on add.

model.description: LEGACY free-text model (shipped clients only). See `make`.

registrationPlate.description: Optional user-entered registration plate (raw). Server trims / collapses internal whitespace / uppercases before storing and enforces the 12-char cap against the NORMALISED value, so a raw string with padding/whitespace is accepted; null / empty clears it. Stored as ≤12 chars (see vehicle.registrationPlate). Format-agnostic (no country regex).

updateVehicleRequest.description: Input for garage.updateVehicle. Identity follows the same two mutually exclusive forms as addVehicleRequest (structured makeId+modelId, or legacy make+model), except that neither is required — a partial edit that touches only a photo or a plate must stay legal. A LEGACY free-text edit CLEARS makeId/modelId/catalogueVersion: text that no longer matches the stored ids would silently corrupt the per-manufacturer counts, so the vehicle drops out of the aggregate rather than lying inside it. On this path a single field (make OR model) may be sent alone, which shipped clients are entitled to do. imagePath sets the COVER photo and must lie under the caller's own vehicleImages/{uid}/{vehicleId}/ prefix (or null to clear all photos); the callable reconciles photoPaths so imagePath === photoPaths[0]. Multi-photo add/remove/reorder go through the dedicated garage.addVehiclePhoto/removeVehiclePhoto/reorderVehiclePhotos callables.

makeId.description: Catalogue manufacturer id, or `other`. Sent together with modelId; re-derives make/model and re-stamps catalogueVersion. Mutually exclusive with make/model.

modelId.description: Catalogue model id within makeId, or `other`. Selecting `other` on a pre-catalogue vehicle KEEPS the existing display text instead of replacing it with a placeholder.

make.description: LEGACY free-text manufacturer (shipped clients). Clears makeId/modelId/catalogueVersion.

model.description: LEGACY free-text model (shipped clients). Clears makeId/modelId/catalogueVersion.

registrationPlate.description: Optional user-entered registration plate (raw). Server trims / collapses internal whitespace / uppercases before storing and enforces the 12-char cap against the NORMALISED value; null / empty clears it. Stored as ≤12 chars (see vehicle.registrationPlate). Format-agnostic (no country regex).

setMainVehicleRequest.description: Input for garage.setMainVehicle. Sets or clears the caller's main-car flag on one owned vehicle; setting also clears the flag on any other currently-main vehicle (max-1 invariant). Re-affirming the existing state is a write-free no-op.

deleteVehicleRequest.description: Input for garage.deleteVehicle. Removes the vehicleImages/{uid}/{vehicleId}/ storage prefix together with the document.

addVehiclePhotoRequest.description: Input for garage.addVehiclePhoto. Records one already-uploaded photo on an owned vehicle: photoPath must lie under the caller's own vehicleImages/{uid}/{vehicleId}/ prefix (one segment below it). Appended to photoPaths; becomes the cover (imagePath) when it is the first photo. Rejected when the vehicle already holds 10 photos (failed-precondition) or the path is already present (already-exists).

removeVehiclePhotoRequest.description: Input for garage.removeVehiclePhoto. Removes photoPath from an owned vehicle's photoPaths and deletes its Storage object; removing the cover promotes the next remaining photo. not-found when the path is not part of the vehicle's gallery.

reorderVehiclePhotosRequest.description: Input for garage.reorderVehiclePhotos. orderedPaths sets the full display order of an owned vehicle's photos and must be a permutation of its current photo set (same members and count); orderedPaths[0] becomes the cover (imagePath). Each path must lie under the caller's own vehicleImages/{uid}/{vehicleId}/ prefix. invalid-argument when it is not a permutation.
